title: The Queen's Throne and the Plot Against Salih

paragraphs.text: Solomon sent the messengers back and said he would come with soldiers whom they could never resist. Then he asked his assembly who could bring the queen's throne before her people arrived. A powerful jinn offered to bring it before Solomon rose from his seat. But a man with knowledge from the Scripture said he could bring it before Solomon's eye could blink. When Solomon saw it in front of him, he said this was a favor from his Lord to test whether he would be grateful. Whoever is grateful benefits himself, and his Lord is Free of need and Generous. He had the throne changed a little to test the queen, and she said it seemed to be hers. What she had worshipped besides Allah had kept her away, because she came from a disbelieving people. When she entered the palace, she thought its glass floor was water. Then she admitted that she had wronged herself, and she submitted with Solomon to Allah.

Allah sent Salih to Thamud, telling them to worship Allah, but they split into two quarrelling groups. He asked why they were rushing toward evil instead of seeking forgiveness. They called him a bad omen, but he replied that their omen was with Allah and that they were being tested. Nine leaders in the city made a secret oath to kill him and his family at night. They planned, and Allah also planned, while they did not realize it. So Allah destroyed them and their people, and their empty houses remain as a sign. He saved those who believed and feared Him.

hardWords.m: a group of people gathered together
a sign of good or bad luck
